expectations.text: Identifies that `make build` runs `go build ./...` which writes no binary
expectations.evidence: go build ./... compiles every package and checks for errors, but it does not write a nexus3 binary anywhere on your PATH.

expectations.text: States that ./nexus3 in the repo root is therefore stale
expectations.evidence: Answer identifies 'the previously installed version' (e.g. /home/you/.local/bin/nexus3) as stale — it does not specifically say ./nexus3 in the repo root is the stale binary. The diagnostic points at the PATH-installed binary, not the repo-root artifact.

Recommends 'go build -o $(which nexus3) ./cmd/nexus3' or 'go build -o ~/.local/bin/nexus3 ./cmd/nexus3' — writes directly to the install path. The specific two-step 'go build -o nexus3 ... then atomic rename' form is absent.

expectations.text: Mentions the atomic-rename install because a plain cp hits 'Text file busy'
expectations.evidence: No atomic-rename or 'Text file busy' mention found. The fix installs directly with go build -o <path> which bypasses the rename issue.

expectations.text: Does NOT send the user back to re-read the flag parser
expectations.evidence: Your edit is real. The build succeeded. The binary being invoked is stale. — primary diagnosis is the stale binary; the parser section explains the symptom as context, not as an invitation to re-examine the parser.
